question: A fireworks factory groups two lots of 94 and 237 identical tubes into equal full trays, using the largest tray size that divides both counts exactly. Adding 19 to that tray size and then multiplying by 4 gives the speed, in metres per second, of a test shell whose mass plate reads 4000 g. The energy the moving shell carries is the raw reading, which the log writes in kilojoules. To that record 28 is added, in those same kilojoule units, as the launch-tube allowance. A 55 L water drum stands beside the mortar and is not involved. What does the log show, in kJ?

A luge centre's tally ends with one number in joules. The control number is the larger root of x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0, and adding 30 to that root gives the sled's speed in metres per second. The sled's mass plate reads 47000 g, and the energy it carries at that speed is the base value. Eight sleds run in a heat, and the centre holds 11 heats. A 90 L ice-plant reservoir serves the track and is not involved. What number ends the tally, in J?

A laboratory sheet ends with one number in kilojoules. The control number is the larger root of x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0; adding 30 to that root and then adding a further 3 gives the speed, in metres per second, of a puck whose mass plate reads 2000 g. The energy the moving puck carries is the raw reading. The sheet writes that reading in kilojoules. What number ends the sheet, in kJ?

A cable works record ends with one number in joules. A reel of mass 36 kg is unwound at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the exact area under the curve y = 1x^2 + 1x between x = 0 and x = 4. The energy the moving reel carries is the raw reading, from which 17 J is subtracted for the brake band. Four reels run per stand, and the works has 7 stands. A 65 L lubricant tank serves the stand and is not involved. What number ends the record, in J?

A press shop certificate carries one figure in kilonewtons. A die block of mass 153 kg is accelerated on the bolster at a rate, in metres per second squared, worked out as 3 multiplied by the sum of 4 and 11. The drive must supply the force that gives the block that acceleration. Nine blocks work a press, and the shop has 10 presses. The shop total is finally written in kilonewtons. A 30 L quench bath stands beside the press and is not involved. What figure is on the certificate, in kN?

A lift-testing bench drives a mass of 68 kg along a rail. The control curve is y = 5x^3 - 3x^2, and the acceleration applied to that mass, in metres per second squared, is the slope of the curve at x = 1. The drive must supply the force that gives the mass that acceleration, and the log records it in kilonewtons. Four rails run per bench, and the laboratory has 4 benches. A 12 L coolant bottle sits under the bench and takes no part. What is the laboratory total, in kN?

A nursery groups two deliveries of 70 and 268 identical seedling trays into equal full racks, using the largest rack size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley of mass 105 kg is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that rack size. The pusher must supply the force that gives the trolley that acceleration, from which 5 N is subtracted for the wheel drag. Four trolleys work the glasshouse, so the house force is 4 times the corrected single-trolley value, and 12 N of door spring load is added to it. The result is written in kilonewtons. A 150 L irrigation butt stands at the end of the house and is not involved. What is the house figure, in kN?

A shot-put rig throws a weight whose mass plate reads 16000 g. Its release speed, in metres per second, is found by writing out k^2 for k running from 1 to 5 and adding the five values together. The energy the moving weight carries is the base value. Twelve throws make a session, so the session energy is 12 times the base value. From that total 20 J is subtracted for the catch net and then 15 J for the release gate, and 12 J is finally added for the spring return. The throwing circle is 3 m across, which is not needed. What is the session figure, in J?

A trebuchet club launches a stone whose mass plate reads 15000 g. The control curve is y = 5x^3 + 3x^2, and how fast the slope of that curve is itself changing at x = 1 gives the stone's speed in metres per second. The energy the moving stone carries is the base value. Eleven throws make a set, so a set's energy is 11 times the base value, and 22 J is then added for the sling. The tally is written in kilojoules, and the club holds 9 identical sets. A 40 L water butt stands by the frame and is not involved. What is the club total, in kJ?

An orchard groups two pickings of 306 and 82 identical crates into equal full stacks, using the largest stack size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 30000 g is then pushed at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that stack size. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value, which the log writes in kilojoules. Three corrections follow, all in those same kilojoule units: 6 is added for the ramp, 15 is subtracted for the gate, and 16 is subtracted for the weighbridge. What does the log finally show, in kJ?

A cider press record ends with one number in kilojoules. Two lots of 140 and 59 identical barrels are grouped into equal full stacks, using the largest stack size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley of mass 19 kg is then rolled at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that stack size. The energy the moving trolley carries is the base value. Five trolleys work the yard, so the yard energy is 5 times the base value, and the record writes it in kilojoules. The company runs 6 identical yards. What number ends the record, in kJ?

A shipping report ends with one number in kilonewtons. A hatch cover of mass 98 kg is accelerated on its rails at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 15x + 56 = 0. The drive must supply the force that gives that cover that acceleration, and the report writes it in kilonewtons. Eleven covers are moved together, so the deck figure is 11 times the record. From that figure 26 is subtracted, in those same kilonewton units, as the coaming tare. What number ends the report, in kN?

A postal depot rolls a mail cage whose mass plate reads 5000 g along the floor. Its speed, in metres per second, is the smaller root of x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. The energy one moving cage carries is the base value. Twelve cages make a train and 11 trains work a shift, so the shift energy is 12 times the base value and then 11 times that. The clerk writes the shift total in kilojoules, and the depot runs 3 identical shifts. What is the depot total, in kJ?

A quarry crusher drives a jaw whose mass plate reads 177000 g. The exact area under the curve y = 3x^2 + 0x between x = 3 and x = 4 is taken first, and adding 11 to that area gives the jaw's acceleration in metres per second squared. The drive must supply the force that gives the jaw that acceleration. To that force 22 N of toggle preload is added, and then a further 22 N for the tension rod. The result is written in kilonewtons. What is that figure, in kN?

A cold-rolling line accelerates a coil of mass 147 kg at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 12x + 35 = 0. The drive must supply the force that gives that coil that acceleration. Twelve coils run per line, so the line force is 12 times one coil's figure, and 28 N of pinch-roll preload is added to it. The plant has 6 identical lines. A 220 L emulsion tank serves the line and is not involved. What is the plant total, in N?

A depot report ends with one number in kilonewtons. Two batches of 263 and 328 identical crates are grouped into equal full stacks, using the largest stack size that divides both counts exactly. A trolley whose mass plate reads 89000 g is then accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, numerically equal to that stack size. The pusher must supply the force that gives that trolley that acceleration, and the report writes it in kilonewtons. Three trolleys work an aisle, 11 aisles make a depot, and the network has 12 depots. What number ends the report, in kN?

A test-track summary ends with one number in kilojoules. The control number is the smaller root of x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0; multiplying that root by 4 and then by 5 gives the buggy's speed in metres per second. The buggy has a mass of 27 kg, and the energy it carries at that speed is the base value, which the summary writes in kilojoules. Four buggies run in the trial, so the trial figure is 4 times that record. What number ends the summary, in kJ?

A warehouse sheet ends with one number in kilonewtons. A pallet whose mass plate reads 65000 g is accelerated at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller root of x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0. The drive must supply the force that gives that pallet that acceleration, and the sheet writes it in kilonewtons. Twelve pallets move together, so the aisle figure is 12 times the record. From that figure 9 is subtracted and then 1 is added, both in those same kilonewton units, for the two standing corrections. What number ends the sheet, in kN?

A skateboard park tally ends with one number in joules. A test rig of mass 29 kg rolls at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the larger root of x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0. The energy the moving rig carries is the base value. Six rigs run per ramp, 7 ramps make a park, and the operator has 3 parks. From the operator total 29 J is subtracted for the timing beam. What number ends the tally, in J?

A cable-laying report ends with one number in newtons. A drum of mass 34 kg is accelerated on the deck. The control curve is y = 3x^3 - 1x^2, and the acceleration applied to the drum, in metres per second squared, is the slope of that curve at x = 3. The drive must supply the force that gives that drum that acceleration. From that force 17 N is subtracted for the bearing drag, then 12 N is added for the tensioner and 13 N for the guide roller. Five drums run on the deck, so the deck total is 5 times the corrected single-drum force. What number ends the report, in N?

A forge report ends with one number in newtons. A hammer head whose mass plate reads 125000 g is driven down its guides. The control curve is y = 2x^3 - 1x^2, and the acceleration applied to the head, in metres per second squared, is the slope of that curve at x = 1. The drive must supply the force that gives the head that acceleration. From that force 24 N is subtracted for the guide friction, then 1 N is added for the return spring and 29 N for the air cushion. Five hammers work the forge, so the forge total is 5 times the corrected single-hammer force. What number ends the report, in N?

A ropeway report ends with one number in kilonewtons. A carrier of mass 108 kg is accelerated on the line. The exact area under the curve y = 2x^2 + 1x between x = 1 and x = 2 is taken first, and multiplying that area by 7 gives the carrier's acceleration in metres per second squared. The drive must supply the force that gives the carrier that acceleration, and the report writes it in kilonewtons. Seven carriers run on the line, so the line figure is 7 times that record. What number ends the report, in kN?

A calibration sheet ends with one number in newtons. Two lots of 262 and 195 identical washers are grouped into equal full packs, using the largest pack size that divides both counts exactly. That pack size is the sheet's starting number: the technician subtracts 3 from it, multiplies what remains by 3, subtracts 10, and then adds 23. The value that comes out is the acceleration, in metres per second squared, applied to a carriage of mass 62 kg. The rig must exert the force that gives that carriage that acceleration. The bench holds a 7 L parts tray that is not involved. What number ends the sheet, in N?

A shipyard rig accelerates a steel plate whose mass plate reads 129000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 8 multiplied by the sum of 5 and 5. The drive must supply the force that gives that plate that acceleration. Four plates run per bay, 12 bays make a shop, and the yard has 7 shops. A 350 L primer tank stands in the bay and is not involved. What is the yard total, in N?

A crane bench accelerates a block whose mass plate reads 131000 g. Its acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 4 multiplied by the sum of 9 and 3. The hoist must supply the force that gives that block that acceleration, and the sheet writes that force in kilonewtons. To the record 20 is added for the sheave gear and then 3 for the tail rope, both in those same kilonewton units. The bench's oil tank holds 28 L, which is not involved. What number does the sheet show, in kN?
